plan: This is a second-price auction (Vickrey auction), where the winner pays the second-highest bid. In this format, the dominant strategy is to bid exactly my true value, regardless of what others bid. Bidding higher than my value risks winning but paying more than the item is worth to me. Bidding lower reduces my chances of winning profitable auctions. Since my value is $27, I should bid $27 to maximize expected profit.

This is a second-price auction with independent private values. In such auctions, the dominant strategy is to bid your true value, since you pay the second-highest bid regardless of your own bid (as long as you win). Bidding above your value risks paying more than the item is worth if I win against a bid between my value and my bid; bidding below reduces chances of winning profitable trades. Therefore, truthful bidding maximizes expected profit.

This is a second-price auction, where the dominant strategy is to bid your true value. Bidding exactly $20 ensures that if I win, I pay the second-highest bid (which will be less than my value, guaranteeing non-negative profit), and if I lose, it's because someone valued it more than me, which is the correct outcome. Bidding higher risks paying more than my value if others bid high; bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities.
